title: Sim-Time vs Wall-Clock
description: sim_clock (Phase 12) is a single mutable row, not a history table, so this dashboard shows the live current state each refresh rather than a stored trend line. It computes, from that one row, how far sim_time SHOULD have advanced since last_wall_checkpoint given speed_multiplier, so a drift/consistency check is still possible without needing new schema.

targets.rawSql: SELECT speed_multiplier FROM sim_clock WHERE id = 1
SELECT sim_time FROM sim_clock WHERE id = 1

panels.title: Sim-Time / Wall-Clock Consistency Check
panels.description: implied_current_sim_time = sim_time + (wall seconds elapsed since last_wall_checkpoint) * speed_multiplier. Compare against the live sim-clock's own advancing sim_time (panel above) to sanity-check the ticker is applying speed_multiplier correctly.

targets.rawSql: SELECT sim_time, to_timestamp(last_wall_checkpoint) AS last_wall_checkpoint, speed_multiplier, EXTRACT(epoch FROM now()) - last_wall_checkpoint AS wall_seconds_since_checkpoint, sim_time + make_interval(secs => (EXTRACT(epoch FROM now()) - last_wall_checkpoint) * speed_multiplier) AS implied_current_sim_time FROM sim_clock WHERE id = 1
